clue.text: Change is needed in this place of entertainment

definitions.text: Change is needed in this place of entertainment

blocks.note: surface reading: a venue that needs renovating or a new direction
setter's reading: change means loose coins, which you feed into the slot machines there

explanation.walkthrough: Change sounds like reform or alteration, but here it is small coins, the currency of slot machines and video games.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside hall full of coin-operated games and slot machines is exactly where pocket coins get spent for fun.

clue.text: Chums in boats get changed into swimwear

indicators.note: things that are changed are altered into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, the verb included

explanation.surface: Friends out on the water change into their swimming gear.
explanation.walkthrough: Get looks like part of the signal, get changed; it is the last word of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathing costumes are garments worn for swimming, so the phrase is a plain synonym for the clothing category.

clue.text: Escort, before sweetheart entered, swore

indicators.note: things that entered something have gone inside it, so these letters sit within the escort word

blocks.note: to escort someone is to guard them
ante is Latin for before, as in antenatal
the heart of the word sweet is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A chaperone made a vow just before a lover came in.
explanation.walkthrough: Sweetheart looks like a lover; it is split as the heart of sweet. Before and sweetheart both go inside the escort word.
explanation.definitionFit: To guarantee something is to give a solemn promise about it, so guaranteed works as a past-tense synonym of swore.

clue.text: Salesman turned up to see red bouquet

indicators.note: in a down entry, turning a word upward makes it read from bottom to top, i.e. backwards

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative
to see red is to be furious, to fume

explanation.surface: A sales rep loses his temper over a bunch of flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: Bouquet looks like flowers, but it is the wine-taster's word for a scent.
explanation.definitionFit: A bouquet is a pleasant smell, especially of wine, so it is a fair synonym for a fragrance or scent.

clue.text: Mark races back, losing a point

indicators.note: going back means the word is read from its end to its start
a point of the compass is dropped, and E for east is the one that goes

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A runner sets a record time in reverse and drops a point in the standings.
explanation.walkthrough: Compass points N, S, E and W are standard crossword letters; removing E from SECAR leaves SCAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a lasting blemish left on skin by a wound, so it is one kind of mark.

clue.text: One undertaking, with unusual care, to find ruler

indicators.note: an unusual arrangement is not the normal one, so the letters are set in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone takes on a task, carefully hunting for a measuring stick or a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: One undertaking reads like someone taking on a job; the pun is on undertaker, another name for the profession.
explanation.definitionFit: An undertaker is a professional arranging burials, so someone in the undertaking trade is the person who runs funerals.

clue.text: You'll hear it said these people are too much in love

definitions.text: these people are too much in love

blocks.clueFragment: these people are too much in love
blocks.note: surface reading: people excessively infatuated
setter's reading: spoken, too sounds like two, so these are pairs of people in love

explanation.walkthrough: Said out loud, too much in love is also two much in love: a pair of sweethearts.
explanation.definitionFit: Couples who are dating are pairs of people romantically attached, which is the two in love the spoken pun gives.

clue.text: I met a rum doctor lacking insight

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are tampered into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone recalls meeting an odd physician who had no understanding.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor looks like a person, the rum doctor met; here it is a verb meaning falsify. Rum is British slang for odd.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone not yet grown up mentally lacks the wisdom and understanding that come with age and experience.

clue.text: Mug against accepting love token

indicators.note: something accepting another thing takes it in, so the love letter goes inside

blocks.note: a mug is a drinking cup
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
leaning against a wall is leaning on it

explanation.surface: A souvenir mug given as a sign of affection.
explanation.walkthrough: Love token looks like one phrase, but love is the letter and token alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A coupon is a voucher exchangeable for goods or a discount, which is what a token is in this sense.

clue.text: Removing front of best girl's book

indicators.note: removing the front means the opening letter of the next word is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
her is the possessive for a girl

explanation.surface: Someone takes the cover off their best friend's novel.
explanation.walkthrough: Book is the definition: ESTHER is a book of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Book of Esther is one of the books of the Hebrew Bible, so it names a specific biblical book.

clue.text: Is patient, but is frightened of holding little brother back

indicators.note: sent back means the short word for a sibling is read from end to start
something holding another thing has it inside, so the sibling goes within

blocks.note: to fear something is to be frightened of it
bro is the short form of brother

explanation.surface: Someone stays calm, though secretly afraid of keeping a younger sibling in check.
explanation.walkthrough: Little brother suggests a younger sibling; here little means shortened, as in bro. Don't confuse the answer with forebears, ancestors.
explanation.definitionFit: To forbear is to hold back or refrain with restraint, which is how a patient person behaves.

clue.text: "Morning" in French is a word of prayer

blocks.note: am, ante meridiem, marks the morning hours
en is the French word for in

explanation.surface: A French greeting at the start of the day offered as a prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: Morning in French looks like a request to translate morning; it is two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is said at the close of a prayer or hymn to express agreement, so it is the standard word ending prayers.

clue.text: Relating to coin collections ICI man must put straight

indicators.note: putting something straight means reorganising it from a muddle, so the letters get reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A worker at a chemicals company is told to sort out the company's coin hoard.
explanation.walkthrough: ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a large British chemicals company.
explanation.definitionFit: Numismatics is the study and collecting of coins and medals, so the adjective describes anything to do with that hobby.

clue.text: Way to declare luggage on flights

blocks.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
to air a view is to declare it publicly
suitcases are luggage

explanation.surface: Instructions for passengers on how to declare bags when travelling by air.
explanation.walkthrough: Flights looks like air travel, alongside luggage and declaring; here it is flights of stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a series of steps between floors, so staircases are flights in the building sense.

clue.text: One admitted having used this?

blocks.note: surface reading: someone confessing they used something
setter's reading: admitted means let in at the door, after rapping on it with the fitting there

explanation.walkthrough: Admitted reads as confessed; it means let into a house after using the door fitting to announce yourself.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor raps the metal fitting on a front door to be let inside, so it is what the admitted caller used.

clue.text: Dressing in black and taking a long time

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
taken as written
an age is a very long time

explanation.surface: Someone slowly getting dressed in black clothes, taking ages about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Dressing in black suggests putting on clothes; dressing is the noun for a wound covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A dressing is a covering applied to a wound, and a strip of gauze wrapped round an injury is the typical one.

clue.text: Prevented Green taking a bearing in time

indicators.note: taking here means having something added on after it
in places the green and bearing pieces inside the time word

blocks.note: vert is green in heraldry
a compass bearing, east
AD, anno domini, labels the time of the Christian era

explanation.surface: A green campaigner, taking his bearings just in time, stopped something happening.
explanation.walkthrough: Vert is the heraldic word for green on coats of arms, and AD, anno domini, stands for a time or era.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert a disaster is to stop it happening, so averted works as a past-tense synonym of prevented.

clue.text: Disregarded what the plane did?

blocks.note: first meaning: ignored, skipped in favour of someone else
second meaning: flew above, literally

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is literal: an aircraft travelling across the sky above you.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ignored for promotion is said to be skipped, and an aircraft flying overhead literally went across above.

clue.text: Source of decay overhead to be included

indicators.note: being included means placed inside the word for decay

blocks.note: rot is decay
the head of the word over is its first letter

explanation.surface: The cause of rot in a building is the overhead roof, which must be dealt with.
explanation.walkthrough: Overhead looks like the roof above; it is split as over plus head, meaning the first letter of over.
explanation.definitionFit: The root of a problem is its origin or cause, so root and source both mean where something comes from.

clue.text: Ring Eric, worried about cup holder

indicators.note: something worried has been agitated and shaken about, so the name's letters are jumbled
about means around, so the jumbled name surrounds the drinking vessel

blocks.note: a ring is round like the letter O
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Phone Eric, who is anxious about the trophy holder.
explanation.walkthrough: Cup holder reads as one phrase, but holder alone is the definition; cup is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An occupier holds or occupies a property or position, so occupier and holder both mean the person in possession.

clue.text: One month I returned frozen

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the letters are read in reverse

blocks.note: Dec is the calendar abbreviation for December
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone came back after a month away to find everything frozen.
explanation.walkthrough: One looks like it should give I; it just goes with month. DEC plus I, reversed, gives ICED.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced means covered in or turned to ice, so iced and frozen are synonyms.

clue.text: Tolerate performance around church piano

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the performance word encloses the other pieces

blocks.note: an act is a performance
CE is the abbreviation for the Church of England
p is the musical marking for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Putting up with a show staged around a church piano.
explanation.walkthrough: Piano here is the musical direction p, meaning soft, not the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept something you dislike is to put up with it, so accept and tolerate are synonyms.

clue.text: Stick had bent before

indicators.note: something bent is twisted out of shape, so the word's letters are twisted into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: A walking stick had been bent earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: Stick looks like a noun, a cane that had bent; it is the verb, to cling.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to cling or remain attached to a surface, so it is a verb synonym for stick.

clue.text: Watches Rose dancing - which may offend the viewers!

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and change places, so the name is rearranged

blocks.note: to eye something is to watch it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rose's dancing is so bad that anyone watching would be offended.
explanation.walkthrough: Watches looks like a noun, timepieces; it is the verb, to eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyesores are ugly sights, things unpleasant to look at, so they offend anyone who sees them.
